proposition.claim:
A star body has a continuous positive radial function \(\rho_K\) on \(S^{n-1}\); its intersection body satisfies \(\rho_{IK}(\theta)=|K\cap\theta^\perp|_{n-1}\). Theorem 1.1 concerns all such bodies in \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\geq3\), satisfying \(I^2K=cK\) for a positive scalar \(c\), and characterizes them as origin-centered ellipsoids. The fixed-point corollary forces a Euclidean ball. Convexity is not an initial hypothesis of the main theorem.

Equation reference: eq:source, eq:bad. On printed page 551, PDF page 43, Section 9.1(4), equation (9.5) is \[h_K^{\,1-p}S_K=c\,d\theta,\qquad p\geq-n,\quad K=-K ,
 \] where \(h_K\) is the support function and \(S_K\) the surface area measure. The immediately following unnumbered display gives \[F_p(K)=\frac1p\int_{S^{n-1}}h_K^p\,d\theta+\frac1c|K|
 \] and asserts that [eq:source] (#eq:source) is its Euler–Lagrange equation under support-function perturbations. For \(p=0\), the parenthetical replacement is the log integral, again with the positive volume term. Both plus signs were checked on the acquired original page.

N: 3. P: 2. C: 1. K: Unit Euclidean ball B^3. Verification: Smooth strictly convex origin-symmetric compact body, h=1>0, S=dtheta, p>=-n; K_t=(1+t)B^3 for |t|<1/2 is an admissible symmetric support perturbation.
